title: Texas's 7th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Texas's 7th Congressional District pits four-term Democratic incumbent Rep. Lizzie Fletcher against Republican nominee Alexander Hale. The district, which covers parts of western Houston and western Harris County including Bellaire and Gulfton, was redrawn in 2025 amid a mid-decade redistricting controversy that reached the Supreme Court. Fletcher, first elected in 2018 when she flipped a longtime Republican-held seat, is seeking re-election in a district that the Cook Political Report rates as Solid Democratic (D+13). Hale, a political newcomer and energy consultant, won a competitive Republican primary runoff in May 2026.
polling_note: No district-specific public opinion polls were found for this race. The Cook Political Report rates the seat as Solid Democratic (D+13 PVI).

candidates.name: Lizzie Pannill Fletcher
candidates.summary: Lizzie Fletcher is the Democratic incumbent representing Texas's 7th Congressional District, first elected in 2018. She serves as Vice Ranking Member on the House Energy and Commerce Committee and is a former litigation partner at AZA law firm. Fletcher has focused on energy policy, health care, infrastructure, and reproductive rights during her tenure in Congress.

candidates.name: Alexander Hale
candidates.summary: Alexander Hale is the Republican nominee for Texas's 7th Congressional District, having won the May 2026 primary runoff. A fourth-generation Houstonian and Baylor University graduate, he works as an Energy and Chemicals Consultant at Alvarez & Marsal. This is his first run for elected office, and he campaigns on a platform of conservative fiscal policy, border security, energy independence, and public safety.
